facts.fact: Development Gateway's diagnostic for UNICEF Lesotho says the OpenEMIS rollout is beginning with a 2018 pilot tracking individual learners in one hundred low-performance schools, attached to a World Bank project; it does not give the schools' level or say who enters the records.
The diagnostic says the Ministry of Education and Training is itself implementing OpenEMIS as its new education information system, in 2018.

The diagnostic says UNICEF is supporting the OpenEMIS rollout and that the 2018 learner-tracking pilot leverages an existing World Bank project (the Lesotho Basic Education Improvement Project); no domestic budget is mentioned.

systems.country_label: OpenEMIS; new Education Management Information System (EMIS) platform

systems.tiers: Being implemented in 2018; a pilot tracking individual learners in one hundred low-performance schools, with the medium-term goal of moving from school facility data to individual learner performance

systems.system: Education Management Information System (EMIS), the existing annual collection

systems.tiers: Annual: school staff collect the data and send it to the district; described as limited to an annual 'snapshot' and as tracking facility, not individual, data

systems.system: National Identity and Civil Registry (NICR) interface with EMIS
systems.tiers: Not in place: early discussion of interfacing NICR with EMIS for individual learner tracking; UNICEF has supported pilots harmonising civil registration and school registration

note: Read as passages. The pilot is classed emis on the document's words 'tracking individual learners' and 'individual learner performance'; it does not say that schools themselves enter the records, which the parent should weigh.
